Iran says Hormuz Strait to remain closed until US meets seven conditions
items.summary: Iran says Hormuz Strait to remain closed until US meets seven conditions Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf has said that the Strait of Hormuz will remain shut until Washington meets certain conditions. Ghalibaf, who also acts as Tehran's chief negotiator in the talks, said that the contested waterway will remain closed until seven conditions based on the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding are met by Washington. He conceded that the US had made "some proposals through a mediator" after Tehran presented a seven-day roadmap to reopen the strait. But he warned Washington that "the era of wasting time and dictating unilateral demands is over" and Iran's position remains "clear and definite".

Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi confirmed they had received a response via intermediaries to their proposal for a seven-day plan to reopen the contested Strait of Hormuz, which they presented at UN meetings in New York. He added that "the Islamic Republic of Iran’s final response is prepared [and] the necessary steps will be taken through the appropriate channels". US President Donald Trump said in late September that he had rejected the plan, but Iran has maintained that negotiations through mediators are ongoing. Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said earlier today that the strait will remain shut until Washington meets seven conditions based on the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding.

items.summary: Iranian rial at new low, as cenbank sells dollars to support currency Iran's rial continued its decline on Saturday, as the central bank announced an injection of up to $2 billion to support the currency while the economy faces US sanctions and a naval blockade. The US dollar was sold at around 2.688 million rials, up from 2.632 million on Friday, according to free-market tracking website bon-bast.com, while alanchand.com reported 2.695 million rials per dollar. State television said state banks began selling up to $2 billion to support the currency, which has lost more than half of its value in the past year. With an inflation rate of more than 70 percent, life is becoming ever tougher for ordinary citizens unable to afford basic necessities or rent ​as a US blockade cuts the state's financial lifeline – oil exports. Many Iranians seeking safe havens for their savings have been buying dollars, other hard currencies or gold.

items.title: Not since 9/11 has the UK faced such a security crisis – and threat to our liberal principles | Gaby Hinsliff
items.summary: The combination of Iranian, Russian and Chinese aggression is deeply worrying: just how much more concerned about security should the country be? The first time the window-rattling roar of a B-1 bomber woke me up this summer, I thought for one crazed second we were under attack. By the second time, I’d learned to recognise the sound of US planes taking off from their base at RAF Fairford for what it was: a reminder that although Britain wants no part in this war with Iran, we cannot quite escape the consequences. We’ll feel them at the petrol pump , or in the supermarket this autumn, or in this winter’s heating bills . But living under the flight path adds an extra edge to it. The skies finally fell silent last week, but only because the bombers have been hastily summoned home after an alleged terrorist plot to attack Fairford, in which (according to the prime minister) there are “ strong indications that Iran played a part ”. items.summary: In September, as the media focused its attention on the conflict in the Strait of Hormuz and the debates at the U.N. General Assembly, some internal developments in Iran went all but unnoticed. On September 28, 32 Iranian conservatives published an open letter calling for Iran to withdraw from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) as a matter of urgency. Since the “ snapback ” of U.N. sanctions on Iran in September 2025, ultraconservative Iranian lawmakers have regularly pushed for pulling out of the NPT, under which the vast majority of states have committed to not develop nuclear weapons. The Majles — Iran’s parliament — drafted a law that would have initiated the move in 2025, but it has yet to move forward. In September, some lawmakers submitted new “triple-urgency” legislation to the Majles ’ president, Mohammad Baqer Ghalibaf, who is also currently Iran’s chief negotiator These continuous calls by ultraconservatives to withdraw from the NPT have yet to produce an actual withdrawal because of a lack of political consensus. items.summary: Last week, after nearly two decades of fighting, the U.S. finally pulled the plug on its seemingly endless war in Iraq. Like our exit from Afghanistan just a few years ago, the end of fighting in Iraq was met with an eerie quiet. It doesn’t take much to figure out why so little attention is paid to the end of these wars: they mark yet another loss for America and the people in Washington who insist our military power can solve every problem, everywhere. Both conflicts are examples of American hubris — strategically incoherent wars fought with American lives at the expense of too many Iraqis and Afghans lives. But, of course, we refuse to learn our lesson. The week before Americans finally vacated Iraq, President Donald Trump took to his proverbial pulpit at the U.N. to brag about his exploitation of Venezuela for oil, declaring “to the victor goes the spoils.” It was a stark expression of how America’s domination of the global order — it’s imperialism, if you will — really works. In practice, each is an excludable asset held by an identifiable actor, and the Iran war has demonstrated that they can be withheld and monetised. The war followed the failure of the most ambitious campaign of economic coercion yet attempted. items.summary: Donald Trump’s unpopularity and the economic struggles of voters have boosted Democrats. But with less than a month to go, there is no complacency For once, Democrats and Donald Trump might be in agreement: “Pretend I’m on the ticket,” the historically unpopular president has instructed supporters . Midterms are in large part a referendum on the incumbent, and Trump’s war on Iran and its impact on the cost of living have boosted support for Democrats. With less than a month to go, they have reason to be upbeat . The party has a mountain to climb after the devastating defeats of 2024, and the gerrymandering of Republicans, but surveys give it a lead of about nine points on the generic ballot, which measures preference for parties rather than specific candidates. Attention has turned from the prospects of seizing the House, where Democrats are forecast a clear majority, to what once seemed like the highly optimistic possibility of taking the Senate too. While the world looks on in dismay at his farcical war in Iran, the thuggery of Ice agents or clownish attacks on erstwhile allies like Canada and Denmark, the core functions of the American government are slowly disintegrating. It is harder to get people to focus on the machinery of the state because the effects are often slow and hard to pin down. Outbreaks of disease – such as the recent wave of explosive diarrhoea across the US – might have happened anyway, but were probably made worse by lay-offs at the Centers for Disease Control. Likewise, Trump is not directly responsible for natural disasters, but response times in the past year may have been hampered by mass redundancies at the National Weather Service. items.summary: In Londen is een nieuwe verdachte aangehouden op verdenking van het voorbereiden van een terroristische aanslag bij de luchtmachtbasis in Fairford. Dat meldt de contraterrorisme-afdeling van de Britse politie. Het gaat om een 22-jarige man met de Britse nationaliteit. In hetzelfde gebied is ook een woning doorzocht. Op 27 september werd alarm geslagen bij een Britse luchtmachtbasis in het graafschap Gloucestershire, nadat er verdachte witte bestelbusjes waren gespot. De politie vreesde dat er explosieven in de witte busjes lagen en woningen werden uit voorzorg ontruimd. Er werden enkel blikken benzine in de busjes gevonden. Op diezelfde dag werden er vijf Britse mannen aangehouden. Later bleek dat een van de verdachten eerder al zelf de politie had gebeld . Op 1 oktober werd nog een verdachte opgepakt. De zes verdachten zijn allemaal in de twintig. Ze mogen verder onderzoek op vrije voeten afwachten. In his first public speech since the US-Israel war on Iran began, Amin Nasser said the conflict reduced oil supply from the region by "nearly 3bn barrels", with over 1bn barrels of oil released from reserves to cushion the depletion. Nasser estimated that "less than 6bn barrels of commercial inventories remain today, with the vast majority not practically available". items.summary: Hormuz Strait disruptions could lead to global food security crisis Disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz could lead to a global food security crisis, the secretary general of the International Chamber of Commerce (ICC), John Denton, warned. According to the Wall Street Journal, Denton indicated that if the vital waterway is not reopened, grain prices could rise by up to 80 percent. The situation in the strait has also caused a shortage of around 2.7 million tons of fertiliser on the world market, a decrease of nearly 40 percent. Such obstacles could affect international agricultural production and food supplies, making import-dependent countries especially vulnerable. The report noted that the ICC is working with the UN and the International Maritime Organization on a mechanism that would transfer temporary management of navigation through the waterway to the UN secretary general. However, the ongoing tensions between the US and Iran have hindered its implementation, the report added.

items.summary: On September 30, the U.S. completed the withdrawal of its troops from Iraq. Heralding this event, Iraq declared “Sovereignty Day,” celebrating the end of U.S. occupation and return of full sovereignty to the people of Iraq. In practice, this withdrawal was little more than the departure of a few hundred soldiers that had returned to Iraq in 2014 – at the invitation of the Iraqi government – to provide support and assistance to the collapsing Iraqi Army in its fight against ISIS. Unlike the hundreds of thousands of troops needed in Germany and Japan at the end of WWII, the troops of Operation Inherent Resolve were neither an occupation nor a challenge to sovereign control. Nonetheless, the mission had become a political liability and a convenient excuse for anti-government militias to maintain independence, retain weapons and force its will both in the streets and within Parliament. items.title: The case for pulling US military back from the first island chain
items.summary: Late last month, Japan’s defense ministry made an unsettling announcement. A U.S. ground-based missile system, known as the Typhon and capable of firing Tomahawk missiles, would not return to the United States after being deployed to Japan for military exercises. Instead, it would be stored at Kadena Air Base in Okinawa, at least temporarily. Tokyo tried to downplay the move, noting that the decision was intended to support training, not warfighting, and that no U.S. Army units would deploy with the missile system. But the reassuring language is unlikely to forestall the negative consequences of the posture change: an increase in military tensions along the first island chain in East Asia. The timing of the decision, following closely on the heels of the visit of Chinese President Xi Jinping to Washington , may seem out of sync with Donald Trump’s “dovish” outreach to Beijing. But the contradiction is a feature, not a bug, of the Trump administration’s Asia policy. items.title: Can Kurds in Iraq unite as US troops withdraw from the country?
items.summary: On September 21, the Kurdistan Region of Iraq officially announced the completion of the long-delayed unification and reorganization of its Peshmerga paramilitary forces under the Ministry of Peshmerga Affairs (MoPA). The Peshmerga are Kurdish armed forces, with roots going back to Kurdish guerrillas who fought as a more or less united front against successive Iraqi governments for most of the 20th century. After the 2003 invasion, though, they never came together as one Kurdish national army. Instead, they split into two separate party forces, the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) and the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP), each tied to one of the region's dominant political factions. Kurdish leaders hailed the September unification announcement as a historic victory for the Kurds in Iraq. Notably, the unification happened nine days before the final U.S. military withdrawal from Iraq. The timing raises an important question: as Washington shrinks its direct military presence in Iraq, what security architecture will it leave behind? items.title: VS haalt bommenwerpers weg uit Engeland vanwege 'dreiging'
items.summary: De Verenigde Staten hebben alle twaalf bommenwerpers weggehaald van de Britse luchtmachtbasis Fairford. Dat zou zijn gebeurd vanwege een nieuwe dreiging die volgens Amerikaanse media afkomstig is van Iran. Vorige week werden er in de buurt van de basis in Fairford vijf Britse mannen aangehouden, die verdacht worden van het voorbereiden van een terroristische aanslag. Later werd nog een verdachte opgepakt. De Britse premier Burnham denkt net als de Amerikaanse president Trump dat Iran erachter zit. The New York Times schrijft dat er opnieuw dreigingen zijn binnengekomen. De krant spreekt van een "door Iran gesteund complot". Halsoverkop zouden de bommenwerpers zijn weggehaald. Een anonieme bron zegt tegen CNN dat het ongebruikelijk is dat bommenwerpers terug naar 'huis' worden gehaald, in plaats van dat ze naar een andere plek in de regio worden verplaatst. Basis gebruikt bij oorlog tegen Iran De bommenwerpers op de basis in Fairford werden door de Verenigde Staten gebruikt om Iran aan te vallen. items.summary: Lebanon seeks 'new chapter' with Iran, prime minister says Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam said on Sunday that Lebanon wants a new chapter in relations with Iran based on mutual respect and non-interference. In an interview with Lebanese broadcaster NBN, Salam stated that he had accepted a meeting requested by Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, saying: "We do not interfere in Iran's affairs." He said Lebanon would prefer Iran to appoint a new ambassador, noting that the current envoy's residence permit had been renewed for three months "as a citizen" but not in his previous diplomatic capacity. Salam also said Lebanon cannot "sit and wait" for a settlement between the US and Iran. "If it happens, that's good. And if it doesn't happen, are we to remain sitting and waiting?" he said. "The state cannot remain in a state of waiting. We must head south and to all regions and bear our responsibilities." items.title: Is China Trump's only hope for ending the Iran war?
items.summary: The current war with Iran and its chaotic unfolding open a door of great danger for the U.S. and the planet. At best, we are condemned to negotiations dominated by personal and political imperatives that seem to fit with a common description of insanity — to keep doing the same thing and expect a different result. At worst, the crisis raises the prospect that tactical nuclear weapons could be employed to solve it. The situation has now become so grave, and its implications for the global economy so devastating, that even China — which otherwise is notoriously disciplined in avoiding entanglement in other countries’ conflicts — has indicated openness to joining a mediation effort to end the conflict. Both China and the U.S. are right to be concerned about the crisis. The two have a mutual interest in solving this problem and keeping it from becoming a worse irritant. items.summary: Three commercial vessels struck in Hormuz since 1 Oct, UKMTO says Attacks on commercial ships witnessed a surge during the past three days, as at least three tankers were struck by unidentified projectiles in and around the Strait of Hormuz, according to United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) warnings. Early Saturday, UKMTO reported that a crude oil tanker was hit on its port side approximately 4 nautical miles east of Oman. A day earlier, an outbound vessel suffered a small fire and blackout, while a second crude tanker was struck nearby. On Thursday, a supertanker carrying 2.5 million barrels caught fire after being hit off Oman while transiting an unauthorised route, according to Iran's Fars news agency. In its weekly Voluntary Reporting Area Overview released on 2 October, UKMTO said 91 incidents of damage to vessels have been reported since February this year. Three tankers have been struck in and around the Strait of Hormuz since 1 October 2026. (AFP)

clusters.headline: Iran's warns 'half-a-century-old' UAE over claim on three Gulf islands

items.title: Iran's warns 'half-a-century-old' UAE over claim on three Gulf islands
items.summary: Iran's warns 'half-a-century-old' UAE over claim on three Gulf islands Ali Akbar Velayati, a senior adviser to Iran's supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei, has warned the United Arab Emirates (UAE) against challenging Tehran and its sovereignty over three islands in the Persian Gulf. In a post on his X account, Velayati dismissed recent claims made by the UAE at the United Nations General Assembly regarding sovereignty over Greater Tunb, Lesser Tunb, and Abu Musa, saying the three islands will remain Iranian forever, according to IRNA. "A country whose political life does not reach half a century makes claims from the UN podium about islands that have been recorded under Iran's name in historical documents and maps of past centuries," Velayati said in the Farsi-language post. He added that the UAE should not "rely on foreign powers" for its security and should instead pursue good relations with its neighbours, IRNA reported. "The neighbour stays, and the guest goes… Regional experience has shown that imported security has an expiration date," said the former Iranian foreign minister.

Nieuwe worden er amper nog verkocht en ook naar tweedehandsauto's is nu nog maar weinig vraag door de hoge dieselprijs. "Die markt is echt geïmplodeerd", zegt Niels Oude Luttikhuis, eigenaar van ikwilvanmijnautoaf.nl. Dat bedrijf bemiddelt tussen consumenten die hun auto willen verkopen en autobedrijven die auto's opkopen. items.summary: On Monday, as the war with Iran crossed the seven-month mark, Governor Greg Abbott declared a statewide disaster in Texas as a result of a massive increase in diesel prices and a deepening fuel shortage. Texas is hardly alone. Diesel prices have climbed nationwide since the war began, with the national average now around $6.45 per gallon , up from $3.76 when the war began in late February, according to data from AAA. A number of other states have recently taken steps to try to ease the costs of gas and diesel amid the ongoing war. As the midterm elections near and the war’s costs hit voters’ wallets, Abbott's declaration is a window into a larger problem for Republicans across the country, including some in deep red states. An increasing number of Republicans are being forced to spend money and political capital defending seats that they carried easily in recent elections. “The Iran War is proving to be a drag on Republicans, even in solidly Republican states,” Brian Darling, a Republican strategist and former counsel to Sen. items.title: War, power games and impunity. I watched the farce that is the UN general assembly: what a tragedy, what a mess | Nesrine Malik
items.summary: Ukraine, Iran, Palestine and Sudan: it has so many problems to confront and fails to do so. Seen up close, it is a study in stasis and decline UN general assembly meetings are not usually riveting occasions. But this year’s encapsulated a world in flux and crisis, an international law and organisation structure that is falling apart, and a humanitarian order machine running hot. What unfolded was less a gathering for resolution and resolve than a display of showboating, frustration and fractiousness. It was a snapshot for the history books of four huge destabilising conflicts for which there seems to be no means of, or interest in, resolution – Ukraine, Iran, Palestine and Sudan. Volodymyr Zelenskyy delivered an account of five years of Russian aggression: the staggering loss of life – hundreds of thousands killed on both sides – the porousness of the sanctions on Russia, the “madness” of it all. clusters.headline: Hegseth says American forces have ‘destroyed’ Iran’s military

items.title: Hegseth says American forces have ‘destroyed’ Iran’s military
items.summary: Hegseth says American forces have ‘destroyed’ Iran’s military Secretary of War Pete Hegseth told a gathering of military leaders at Quantico Marine base on Wednesday that US forces have “destroyed” Iran’s navy, air force, defence systems, leadership and military-industrial capacity. Hegseth praised the American troops he addressed, crediting them with having destroyed Iran’s “entire defense space”. “Iran’s conventional shield has been crippled, and their nuclear ambitions have been crippled and laid bare for the world,” he added. Hegseth said the Pentagon has undergone a “clear break” from its past, with a “singular mission” of war-fighting. He said the department had fired “nearly 10 percent of the generals and admirals across the force”, a figure he framed as “accountability” rather than a “purge”, as some media have called it. US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth gives an address at Marine Corps Base Quantico, on 30 September 2026 (Alex Wong/AFP)

items.summary: Nato chief calls US war on Iran ‘absolutely essential’ Nato secretary general Mark Rutte said that it was “absolutely essential for the United States to take on Iran” in an interview at the Euronews Defence and Space summit on Wednesday. Only the US was “capable of taking out the nuclear capability of Iran”, Rutte said, describing the country's nuclear programme as a potential near-term threat “not only for Israel and the Middle East” but for Europe as well. While conceding that the Iran war had its “downsides”, he added that extra defence investments will enable European countries to “take care of their backyard themselves”. “It should be us taking care of the Houthis and the Red Sea”, rather than the US, Rutte said.

items.summary: On the morning of September 24, Abdel Fattah Burhan should have been standing at the podium of the United Nations General Assembly in New York. Instead, he was in Khartoum. The general who leads Sudan’s army and chairs its Sovereignty Council had been offered his American visa on a condition, which, as detailed by Reuters, involved signing the 90-day ceasefire that Massad Boulos, President Donald Trump’s adviser for Arab and African affairs, had been pitching for months. Burhan rejected the condition, telling a crowded stadium in Khartoum on September 26 that “we do not want a visa to any country...we will stay here with you until we die here in this country.” This episode caps a year in which American policy toward Sudan’s civil war has steadily become more hostile toward Burhan and his Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) — the very party that Boulos in a May interview called the “constitutional institution” that must be preserved. items.summary: The Iraq War was already four-years-old when I walked down the ramp of a C-17 at Al Taqaddum Air Base in April 2007. The fact that I am writing these words is proof that I survived that deployment and a subsequent one to Afghanistan in 2013. In the years since, I transitioned back into civilian life, established a new career, and saw my kids grow up and escape the nest. During nearly all of that time, there were still American troops on the ground in Iraq. I have a son serving in the military today. items.title: Venezuela blowback may have a long fuse. It always does.
items.summary: In 1927, Augusto Cesar Sandino began an insurgent campaign against the U.S. occupation of Nicaragua. Under orders from President Calvin Coolidge, the U.S. Marines had intervened in Nicaragua to settle a civil war between a conservative government and liberal rebels. In his manifesto , Sandino responded by effectively declaring war on the United States. He also specifically denounced former liberal leaders who had agreed to put down their arms in the face of U.S. intervention. Speaking of General Moncada, the leading liberal officer who had agreed to end his revolt in talks convened by future Secretary of State Henry Stimson, Sandino wrote: “Nobody gave him the authority to abandon the ranks of the revolution to make secret agreements with the enemy.” One imagines there are Chavistas in Venezuela with similar feelings about interim President Delcy Rodriguez right now. Having intervened to end the civil war in Nicaragua, the U.S. soon found itself embroiled in a bitter counter-insurgency campaign against Sandino’s men. items.summary: The Bunker appears originally at the Project on Government Oversight and is republished here with permission. The U.S. ended its military campaign in Iraq on September 30, as the final American combat troops based there left the country. Their departure ended 23 years of fitful fighting. They found no weapons of mass destruction , which was the battering ram President George W. Bush and his combative coterie used to scaremonger the U.S to invade in 2003. items.title: Not since 9/11 has the UK faced such a security crisis – and threat to our liberal principles | Gaby Hinsliff
items.summary: The combination of Iranian, Russian and Chinese aggression is deeply worrying: just how much more concerned about security should the country be? The first time the window-rattling roar of a B-1 bomber woke me up this summer, I thought for one crazed second we were under attack. By the second time, I’d learned to recognise the sound of US planes taking off from their base at RAF Fairford for what it was: a reminder that although Britain wants no part in this war with Iran, we cannot quite escape the consequences. We’ll feel them at the petrol pump , or in the supermarket this autumn, or in this winter’s heating bills . But living under the flight path adds an extra edge to it. The skies finally fell silent last week, but only because the bombers have been hastily summoned home after an alleged terrorist plot to attack Fairford, in which (according to the prime minister) there are “ strong indications that Iran played a part ”. items.summary: In September, as the media focused its attention on the conflict in the Strait of Hormuz and the debates at the U.N. General Assembly, some internal developments in Iran went all but unnoticed. On September 28, 32 Iranian conservatives published an open letter calling for Iran to withdraw from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) as a matter of urgency. Since the “ snapback ” of U.N. sanctions on Iran in September 2025, ultraconservative Iranian lawmakers have regularly pushed for pulling out of the NPT, under which the vast majority of states have committed to not develop nuclear weapons. The Majles — Iran’s parliament — drafted a law that would have initiated the move in 2025, but it has yet to move forward. In September, some lawmakers submitted new “triple-urgency” legislation to the Majles ’ president, Mohammad Baqer Ghalibaf, who is also currently Iran’s chief negotiator These continuous calls by ultraconservatives to withdraw from the NPT have yet to produce an actual withdrawal because of a lack of political consensus. items.title: Will Americans ever escape this 'imperialist realism'?

Like our exit from Afghanistan just a few years ago, the end of fighting in Iraq was met with an eerie quiet. It doesn’t take much to figure out why so little attention is paid to the end of these wars: they mark yet another loss for America and the people in Washington who insist our military power can solve every problem, everywhere. Both conflicts are examples of American hubris — strategically incoherent wars fought with American lives at the expense of too many Iraqis and Afghans lives. But, of course, we refuse to learn our lesson. The Iran-aligned Houthis took responsibility earlier for a flurry of attacks that included firing a ballistic missile at Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, as the conflict deepens with Saudi Arabia, which backs Yemen's government. "On Tuesday and Wednesday... Abha International Airport and King Khalid International Airport were subjected to attacks targeting their facilities," the kingdom's civil aviation authority said in a statement, without blaming anyone for the attacks. An Egyptian and an Algerian national were killed at Abha airport, and a Sudanese national was killed at the airport in Riyadh, the agency said, with 36 people wounded in the attacks.

items.title: The Guardian view on the US midterms: the cost of living is on the ballot, but this is about democracy too | Editorial
items.summary: Donald Trump’s unpopularity and the economic struggles of voters have boosted Democrats. But with less than a month to go, there is no complacency For once, Democrats and Donald Trump might be in agreement: “Pretend I’m on the ticket,” the historically unpopular president has instructed supporters . Midterms are in large part a referendum on the incumbent, and Trump’s war on Iran and its impact on the cost of living have boosted support for Democrats. With less than a month to go, they have reason to be upbeat . The party has a mountain to climb after the devastating defeats of 2024, and the gerrymandering of Republicans, but surveys give it a lead of about nine points on the generic ballot, which measures preference for parties rather than specific candidates. Attention has turned from the prospects of seizing the House, where Democrats are forecast a clear majority, to what once seemed like the highly optimistic possibility of taking the Senate too. items.title: Blockers by Michael Lewis review – the quiet heroes who tried to stop Doge
items.summary: The author of Moneyball brings his exceptional narrative skills to bear on Musk’s anti-government crusade Donald Trump’s catastrophic errors get so much attention that his systemic ones can easily be missed. While the world looks on in dismay at his farcical war in Iran, the thuggery of Ice agents or clownish attacks on erstwhile allies like Canada and Denmark, the core functions of the American government are slowly disintegrating. It is harder to get people to focus on the machinery of the state because the effects are often slow and hard to pin down. Outbreaks of disease – such as the recent wave of explosive diarrhoea across the US – might have happened anyway, but were probably made worse by lay-offs at the Centers for Disease Control. Likewise, Trump is not directly responsible for natural disasters, but response times in the past year may have been hampered by mass redundancies at the National Weather Service. Cuts to tax collection also seem to have reduced revenue by multiple billions, though we cannot be sure of the causal relationship. Continue reading...

items.title: US and several allies say Iran committed 'terrorist actions'
items.summary: US and several allies say Iran committed 'terrorist actions' The US and nine other countries across the Americas in a joint statement condemned what they called Iran's "terrorist actions". The joint statement was released by the US and endorsed by Argentina, Canada, Colombia, Costa Rica, Dominican Republic, Guyana, Paraguay, Peru, and Trinidad and Tobago. "On 5 October, the undersigned nations, condemn the terrorist actions and other malign influence operations in our hemisphere by Iran and its terrorist proxies," it read. "These hostile efforts include a range of Iranian and proxy-sponsored lethal plotting, illicit fundraising, political interference and foreign influence activities, and operations meant to bolster terrorist networks, coerce perceived enemies, compromise legal or administrative processes, and harm regional security." The joint statement indicated that the countries "stand united" against "such threats", demanding that Tehran and "its proxies must halt these actions now".

items.title: Saudi Aramco chief warns of 'scarily thin’ global oil stockpiles, amid war on Iran
items.summary: Saudi Aramco chief warns of 'scarily thin’ global oil stockpiles, amid war on Iran The chief executive of Saudi Aramco warned that the world's oil stockpiles are now "scarily thin". In his first public speech since the US-Israel war on Iran began, Amin Nasser said the conflict reduced oil supply from the region by "nearly 3bn barrels", with over 1bn barrels of oil released from reserves to cushion the depletion. Nasser estimated that "less than 6bn barrels of commercial inventories remain today, with the vast majority not practically available". "The system is already straining," he told the Energy Intelligence Forum conference in London. "And with precious little else the world can turn to, the supply resilience cushion is scarily thin."

items.title: Hormuz Strait disruptions could lead to global food security crisis
items.summary: Hormuz Strait disruptions could lead to global food security crisis Disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz could lead to a global food security crisis, the secretary general of the International Chamber of Commerce (ICC), John Denton, warned. According to the Wall Street Journal, Denton indicated that if the vital waterway is not reopened, grain prices could rise by up to 80 percent. The situation in the strait has also caused a shortage of around 2.7 million tons of fertiliser on the world market, a decrease of nearly 40 percent. Such obstacles could affect international agricultural production and food supplies, making import-dependent countries especially vulnerable. The report noted that the ICC is working with the UN and the International Maritime Organization on a mechanism that would transfer temporary management of navigation through the waterway to the UN secretary general. However, the ongoing tensions between the US and Iran have hindered its implementation, the report added.

items.title: Despite war US military is leaving a stronger Iraq behind
items.summary: On September 30, the U.S. completed the withdrawal of its troops from Iraq. Heralding this event, Iraq declared “Sovereignty Day,” celebrating the end of U.S. occupation and return of full sovereignty to the people of Iraq. In practice, this withdrawal was little more than the departure of a few hundred soldiers that had returned to Iraq in 2014 – at the invitation of the Iraqi government – to provide support and assistance to the collapsing Iraqi Army in its fight against ISIS. Unlike the hundreds of thousands of troops needed in Germany and Japan at the end of WWII, the troops of Operation Inherent Resolve were neither an occupation nor a challenge to sovereign control. Nonetheless, the mission had become a political liability and a convenient excuse for anti-government militias to maintain independence, retain weapons and force its will both in the streets and within Parliament. While some voices in Washington argue for a keeping residual military presence , the reasonable solution is shifting to a diplomatic and development effort. Instead, it would be stored at Kadena Air Base in Okinawa, at least temporarily. items.title: Can Kurds in Iraq unite as US troops withdraw from the country?
items.summary: On September 21, the Kurdistan Region of Iraq officially announced the completion of the long-delayed unification and reorganization of its Peshmerga paramilitary forces under the Ministry of Peshmerga Affairs (MoPA). The Peshmerga are Kurdish armed forces, with roots going back to Kurdish guerrillas who fought as a more or less united front against successive Iraqi governments for most of the 20th century. After the 2003 invasion, though, they never came together as one Kurdish national army. Instead, they split into two separate party forces, the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) and the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP), each tied to one of the region's dominant political factions. Kurdish leaders hailed the September unification announcement as a historic victory for the Kurds in Iraq. Notably, the unification happened nine days before the final U.S. military withdrawal from Iraq. Dat zou zijn gebeurd vanwege een nieuwe dreiging die volgens Amerikaanse media afkomstig is van Iran. Vorige week werden er in de buurt van de basis in Fairford vijf Britse mannen aangehouden, die verdacht worden van het voorbereiden van een terroristische aanslag. Later werd nog een verdachte opgepakt. De Britse premier Burnham denkt net als de Amerikaanse president Trump dat Iran erachter zit. The New York Times schrijft dat er opnieuw dreigingen zijn binnengekomen. De krant spreekt van een "door Iran gesteund complot". Halsoverkop zouden de bommenwerpers zijn weggehaald. Een anonieme bron zegt tegen CNN dat het ongebruikelijk is dat bommenwerpers terug naar 'huis' worden gehaald, in plaats van dat ze naar een andere plek in de regio worden verplaatst. items.title: Iranian oil minister steps down
items.summary: Iranian oil minister steps down Iran's oil minister Mohsen Paknejad has resigned, the president's office said in a statement on Sunday, amid long queues at petrol stations caused by the ongoing war and US sanctions. Government spokesperson Mehdi Tabatabaei told state TV later on Sunday that Paknejad, a member of President Pezeshkian's cabinet since August 2024, resigned for personal reasons "a long time ago." Hamid Bord, the CEO of the National Iranian Oil Company (NIOC), "has been appointed as acting Minister of Oil by a decree from the president", according to a statement carried by Iran’s state media. Bord has held senior positions at NIOC and previously headed several of its operating units, including the National Iranian South Oil Company and the Iranian Offshore Oil Company.

items.title: Iran airlines resume flights to Iraq’s Najaf after US exemption
items.summary: Iran airlines resume flights to Iraq’s Najaf after US exemption Iranian airlines resumed flights to Iraq ’s Najaf on Sunday after the United States granted Baghdad an exemption allowing sanctioned Iranian carriers to operate to the city holy to Shia Muslims, AFP reported. On Friday, the Iraqi government said it had secured an agreement with the US allowing Iranian airlines, except Mahan Air, to operate 40 daily flights to and from Najaf. Last month, Iraq enforced the US ban on Iranian carriers, especially at Najaf’s airport, which is a major hub for Iranian flights. The US also granted Iraqi Airways, the national carrier, a waiver to fly between Najaf and Iran, with the flights expected to start this month.

Ghalibaf, who also acts as Tehran's chief negotiator in the talks, said that the contested waterway will remain closed until seven conditions based on the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding are met by Washington. items.title: Iran's warns 'half-a-century-old' UAE over claim on three Gulf islands
items.summary: Iran's warns 'half-a-century-old' UAE over claim on three Gulf islands Ali Akbar Velayati, a senior adviser to Iran's supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei, has warned the United Arab Emirates (UAE) against challenging Tehran and its sovereignty over three islands in the Persian Gulf. In a post on his X account, Velayati dismissed recent claims made by the UAE at the United Nations General Assembly regarding sovereignty over Greater Tunb, Lesser Tunb, and Abu Musa, saying the three islands will remain Iranian forever, according to IRNA. "A country whose political life does not reach half a century makes claims from the UN podium about islands that have been recorded under Iran's name in historical documents and maps of past centuries," Velayati said in the Farsi-language post. He added that the UAE should not "rely on foreign powers" for its security and should instead pursue good relations with its neighbours, IRNA reported. "The neighbour stays, and the guest goes… Regional experience has shown that imported security has an expiration date," said the former Iranian foreign minister.

A spokesperson for Yemen's armed forces, which are aligned with the internationally recognised government, said forces were targeting what he described as "vital targets", without providing further details. Yemen's Houthi-run Al Masirah TV reported earlier an attack it said was carried out by Saudi Arabia on Sanaa. There was no immediate Saudi confirmation on the report. The conflict between the Iran-backed Houthis and forces aligned with the Saudi-backed government mostly stopped after a 2022 truce, but fighting has broken out again in a spillover from the wider war between Iran and the United States. Hostilities resumed this year after the Houthis declared a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia in July and began attacking Saudi territory and shipping, while Houthi forces also made major territorial gains along Yemen's Red Sea coast. items.title: State Department says Iranian UN delegation duo expelled from US
items.summary: State Department says Iranian UN delegation duo expelled from US The United States has expelled two members of the Iranian delegation who attended the recent UN General Assembly after they ignored an order to leave the country, the State Department said Saturday. "Two more members of the Iranian delegation were found still in (New York) long after the United Nations General Assembly had passed. They have now been kicked out of the US," a US official told AFP, adding that Secretary of State Marco Rubio "means business." US media reported the State Department had told Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and his delegation to leave the country Monday, and resorted to expelling the two members after learning from the Iranian mission to the UN they remained in the country on Friday. One member of the delegation left Friday night, while the second departed Saturday morning, according to Axios.

items.summary: Iranian rial at new low, as cenbank sells dollars to support currency Iran's rial continued its decline on Saturday, as the central bank announced an injection of up to $2 billion to support the currency while the economy faces US sanctions and a naval blockade. The US dollar was sold at around 2.688 million rials, up from 2.632 million on Friday, according to free-market tracking website bon-bast.com, while alanchand.com reported 2.695 million rials per dollar. State television said state banks began selling up to $2 billion to support the currency, which has lost more than half of its value in the past year. With an inflation rate of more than 70 percent, life is becoming ever tougher for ordinary citizens unable to afford basic necessities or rent ​as a US blockade cuts the state's financial lifeline – oil exports. Many Iranians seeking safe havens for their savings have been buying dollars, other hard currencies or gold.

items.title: L'Inde et sa stratégie de corridors
items.summary: En Inde, dès que l'on parle de sanctions contre la Russie ou bien l'Iran, c'est le transport qui en paye le prix. Fin septembre, le président américain Donald Trump a renforcé sa loi sur les tarifs douaniers contre la Russie. Ces sanctions s'adressent aussi à tous les pays qui commercent avec Moscou. Or, l'Inde, pénalisée par la guerre au Moyen-Orient et la fermeture du détroit d'Ormuz, a continué d'importer du pétrole russe. Dans ses derniers articles pour l'Institut de relations internationales et stratégiques (Iris), Olivier Da Lage, ancien journaliste à RFI et spécialiste de l'Inde, explique comment le pays cherche à bâtir de nouvelles routes pour diversifier son commerce.

items.title: Iraq given US exemption for Iranian flights to and from holy city
items.summary: Iraq given US exemption for Iranian flights to and from holy city The United States has granted sanctions exemptions for some Iranian airlines to operate flights to Iraq's holy city of Najaf, the Iraqi prime minister's office said on Friday. It said Baghdad had secured "an agreement allowing Iranian airlines, with the exception of Mahan Air, to operate 40 flights daily to and from Najaf" , a city sacred to Shia Muslims. The 51 year-old, identified as Ashton Hamed Ellaboudy, is a US Energy Department employee. "As alleged, a US government employee travelled overseas and used his specialised expertise in an attempt to aid the Houthis, a designated Foreign Terrorist Organization backed by Iran," the assistant attorney general for national security, John A Eisenberg, said. Eisenberg claimed that Ellaboudy "acquired materials for the construction of explosive material and drones capable of delivering these explosives". "These allegations are so deeply disturbing that they almost defy imagination," he added. Ellaboudy is scheduled to appear before a federal judge on 2 October in Washington.

Ook zijn volgens de Britse autoriteiten twee panden in hetzelfde gebied doorzocht. In het onderzoek is ook een 26-jarige Brit verhoord. Afgelopen zondag werden vijf Britse mannen, tussen de 23 en 25 jaar, aangehouden in de buurt van de basis van de Royal Air Force bij Fairford in het graafschap Gloucestershire. Ze worden verdacht van het voorbereiden van een terroristische aanslag. Op de luchtmachtbasis zijn naast Britse militairen ook Amerikaanse militairen en bommenwerpers gestationeerd. items.title: Saudi-led coalition claims Houthis targeted power station in Medina
items.summary: Saudi-led coalition claims Houthis targeted power station in Medina The Saudi-led pro-government coalition in Yemen has claimed that the Houthi rebel group targeted a power centre in Medina in a drone attack on Tuesday, damaging one transformer but leaving the overall electricity network unaffected. Medina, in Saudi Arabia's western Hejaz region, is among the holiest cities in Islam. The Houthis, officially called Ansar Allah, have seized territory in Yemen's southwest this month in a rapid offensive triggered by the Saudi bombing of Sanaa airport in July. The group has also bombed the Saudi East-West oil pipeline, through which Riyadh has diverted oil exports amid Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz. But the Houthis previously denied Saudi claims that they had targeted Mecca, the holiest place in Islam.

items.title: War, power games and impunity. I watched the farce that is the UN general assembly: what a tragedy, what a mess | Nesrine Malik
items.summary: Ukraine, Iran, Palestine and Sudan: it has so many problems to confront and fails to do so. Seen up close, it is a study in stasis and decline UN general assembly meetings are not usually riveting occasions. But this year’s encapsulated a world in flux and crisis, an international law and organisation structure that is falling apart, and a humanitarian order machine running hot. What unfolded was less a gathering for resolution and resolve than a display of showboating, frustration and fractiousness. It was a snapshot for the history books of four huge destabilising conflicts for which there seems to be no means of, or interest in, resolution – Ukraine, Iran, Palestine and Sudan. Volodymyr Zelenskyy delivered an account of five years of Russian aggression: the staggering loss of life – hundreds of thousands killed on both sides – the porousness of the sanctions on Russia, the “madness” of it all. items.title: UK PM says 'strong indications' Iran involved in airbase scare
items.summary: UK PM says 'strong indications' Iran involved in airbase scare British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Wednesday there were "strong indications" that Iran was involved in suspicious activity at a UK airbase that triggered a major security incident. "There are strong indications that Iran played a part in what happened over the weekend at RAF Fairford," Burnham told the BBC in an interview, referring to suspected bomb threat near the airbase in southwest England, which is used by the US military in its campaign against Tehran. Iran has denied involvement in the incident, and the five men arrested on suspicion of terrorist offences were later released on bail, with counterterrorism police saying that no improvised explosive devices were found in their vehicle, but a quantity of petrol was discovered.

items.title: Gen. Burhan digs in as Trump's visa-for-ceasefire scheme blows up
items.summary: On the morning of September 24, Abdel Fattah Burhan should have been standing at the podium of the United Nations General Assembly in New York. Instead, he was in Khartoum. The general who leads Sudan’s army and chairs its Sovereignty Council had been offered his American visa on a condition, which, as detailed by Reuters, involved signing the 90-day ceasefire that Massad Boulos, President Donald Trump’s adviser for Arab and African affairs, had been pitching for months. Burhan rejected the condition, telling a crowded stadium in Khartoum on September 26 that “we do not want a visa to any country...we will stay here with you until we die here in this country.” This episode caps a year in which American policy toward Sudan’s civil war has steadily become more hostile toward Burhan and his Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) — the very party that Boulos in a May interview called the “constitutional institution” that must be preserved. items.title: Goodnight Baghdad: US troops leave Iraq after 23 years
items.summary: The Iraq War was already four-years-old when I walked down the ramp of a C-17 at Al Taqaddum Air Base in April 2007. The fact that I am writing these words is proof that I survived that deployment and a subsequent one to Afghanistan in 2013. In the years since, I transitioned back into civilian life, established a new career, and saw my kids grow up and escape the nest. During nearly all of that time, there were still American troops on the ground in Iraq. I have a son serving in the military today. He has never been to Iraq, but I can absolutely sympathize with the Iraq veterans who came home from the war only to see their sons or daughters deploy to the same war zone. items.title: Venezuela blowback may have a long fuse. It always does.
items.summary: In 1927, Augusto Cesar Sandino began an insurgent campaign against the U.S. occupation of Nicaragua. Under orders from President Calvin Coolidge, the U.S. Marines had intervened in Nicaragua to settle a civil war between a conservative government and liberal rebels. In his manifesto , Sandino responded by effectively declaring war on the United States. He also specifically denounced former liberal leaders who had agreed to put down their arms in the face of U.S. intervention. Speaking of General Moncada, the leading liberal officer who had agreed to end his revolt in talks convened by future Secretary of State Henry Stimson, Sandino wrote: “Nobody gave him the authority to abandon the ranks of the revolution to make secret agreements with the enemy.” One imagines there are Chavistas in Venezuela with similar feelings about interim President Delcy Rodriguez right now. Having intervened to end the civil war in Nicaragua, the U.S. soon found itself embroiled in a bitter counter-insurgency campaign against Sandino’s men.
